title: Samsung Electronics Plunges 11% in Premarket, Breaks Below 200,000 Won; SK Hynix Tumbles 13%
text:

 Add preferred source South Korean semiconductor stocks plunged in premarket trading after Democrats won the US midterm elections, raising the prospect of AI data center regulation. Samsung Electronics fell more than 11%, breaking below the 200,000-won mark, while SK Hynix dropped around 14%. The direct trigger was the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index's overnight collapse of more than 12%. Anxiety was heightened by the election of data center regulation supporters in key hubs such as Texas. Still, some analysts caution that with the scope of regulation not yet finalized, investors should watch for the possibility of overselling. Key Elements 
 Samsung Electronics SK Hynix Philadelphia Semiconductor Index Nextrade James Talarico Kiwoom Securities SK Square LG Energy Solution Samsung Electro-Mechanics Nvidia Micron South Korean large-cap semiconductor stocks tumbled together in premarket trading after Democrats scored a landslide victory in the US midterm elections, bringing the possibility of regulations on artificial intelligence (AI) data center construction into focus. Samsung Electronics broke below the 200,000-won mark and SK Hynix fell nearly 14%, with selling spreading across the market's largest stocks by market capitalization.
 According to Nextrade on the 6th, Samsung Electronics (005930) was trading at 178,000 won (approximately $130) in premarket trading as of 8:20 a.m., down 23,300 won (11.56%) from the previous session. At the same time, SK Hynix (000660) stood at 1.082 million won (approximately $800), down 182,000 won (14.40%). Other top Kospi stocks by market cap—SK Square (-14.59%), Samsung Electro-Mechanics (-15.47%), and LG Energy Solution (-7.08%)—also posted sharp declines across the board.
 The day's plunge was directly triggered by the technology selloff on Wall Street overnight. The Dow and the S&P 500 fell 3.44% and 4.36%, respectively, while the Nasdaq dropped 5.52%. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged 12.25%, its biggest drop in six years since March 2020. AI-related stocks closed lower across the board, including Nvidia (-9.26%), Micron (-17.46%), Broadcom (-10.43%), and CoreWeave (-9.83%).
 The market is taking note that, with Democrats seizing both the Senate and the House, a large number of candidates who have publicly backed AI data center regulation were elected. James Talarico, elected as a Democratic senator from Texas for the first time in more than 30 years, is a leading supporter of data center regulation. Texas is a key hub accounting for about 27% of all US data center construction. As Democratic candidates made gains in governorships in major investment regions such as Texas, Georgia, and Ohio, the possibility of permitting delays over power and water use also came into focus.
 Semiconductor stocks had already shown weakness in the previous day's regular session. On the 5th, Samsung Electronics closed at 201,500 won (approximately $150) on the Korea Exchange, down 16,500 won (7.57%) from the prior close, after falling below the 200,000-won mark during the session. It was the first time Samsung Electronics' share price had fallen below 200,000 won in about seven months, since April 13. SK Hynix also ended at 1.264 million won (approximately $930), down 132,000 won (9.46%).
 Still, some analysts say excessive selling should be treated with caution, given that regulation has not yet reached the stage of becoming reality. Han Ji-young, an analyst at Kiwoom Securities, said, "With neither the specific scope of regulation nor any decline in AI demand confirmed, the recent collapse in AI-related stocks appears to be more than overselling." He added, "It is necessary to check whether US hyperscaler companies change their capital expenditure (CAPEX) investment plans and whether 2028 consensus estimates for semiconductor stocks at home and abroad are revised downward."
 The key variable in this situation is the direction of US policy. If Democrats control both the executive branch and Congress, permitting procedures for data center power and water could be tightened, which could slow the pace of AI infrastructure investment and directly affect semiconductor demand forecasts. Conversely, if regulatory legislation does not take concrete shape or hyperscalers maintain their investment plans, the current decline could be reversed as short-term overselling. South Korean semiconductor stocks have earnings heavily tied to demand for high-value-added products such as high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for AI servers, so the market's assessment of the pace of US data center construction is expected to determine the direction of share prices.
